channel.title: The Picky Reader — New Releases
channel.description: New and notable theology releases, tracked weekly.

item.title: The Gospels Are Reliable History — Craig S. Keener
item.description: Drawing on cutting-edge research in genre and memory studies, Keener demonstrates that the Synoptic Gospels function as ancient biographies, accounts deeply concerned with preserving historical information about…

item.title: 10 Questions About Growing in Christ — William R. Osborne
item.description: Thirty readings on prayer, Bible reading, church, hard times, and feeling not good enough.

item.title: The Greatest Project in Space — Markus Motum
item.description: How the International Space Station was built piece by piece in orbit and how astronauts live and work there.

item.title: Whale Song — Nicola Davies, illus. Britta Teckentrup
item.description: How humpback whales learn songs from one another and carry them across the oceans.

item.title: I Wonder If I'm Growing — Raffi, illus. Jon Klassen
item.description: A young child is told they are growing but can't see it happening, and watches for signs of it at home. Based on Raffi's song.

item.title: The Boy Behind the Wardrobe — Suzanne Poulter Harris, illus. Mira Miroslavova
item.description: A picture-book biography of C.S. Lewis, from his childhood and school years to his friendship with Tolkien and the writing of Narnia.

item.title: Bird Men — A. J. Baime
item.description: A. J. Baime tells how the B-29 Superfortress and American air power were built, largely through General Hap Arnold, from the interwar Army Air Corps to the atomic missions.

item.title: Thriving in Lifelong Ministry — Joel R. Beeke
item.description: Beeke draws on nearly fifty years in the pastorate to show how a minister stays spiritually alive across decades: personal piety, family, preaching, leadership, health, and perseverance through opposition. Twelve chapters aimed at pastors who want to finish well rather than merely survive.

item.title: Pain and Paradox in 2 Corinthians — B. G. White
item.description: B. G. White's Durham doctoral study of 2 Corinthians argues that Paul's strength-in-weakness is not just apostolic self-defense but a pattern for ministry itself. An academic monograph, but one with a pastoral payoff.

item.title: The World Made Right — Michael Rowntree
item.description: Michael Rowntree reads Revelation as pastoral encouragement rather than a decoder ring - a book about the exalted Christ and the confident hope of his church. Clear, non-sensational, and refreshingly free of newspaper eschatology.

item.title: Commentary on Isaiah — Theodoret of Cyrrhus; ed. & trans. Gerald Bray
item.description: The first complete English translation of Theodoret of Cyrrhus on Isaiah, edited and translated by Gerald Bray in the Ancient Christian Texts series. A fifth-century Antiochene reading of the prophet, with the sober literal exegesis that school was known for.

item.title: Apologetics at the Cross, Second Edition — Joshua D. Chatraw & Mark D. Allen
item.description: The revised edition of the standard textbook on cross-shaped apologetics: winsome, humble, and anchored in the gospel rather than in winning arguments. Chatraw and Allen have taught a generation of pastors how to defend the faith without losing its heart.

item.title: The Six Minute War — Michael Dobbs
item.description: The 1983 near-misses — Flight 007, a false alarm over Moscow, Able Archer — and Dobbs's question: have we already handed the decision to machines?

item.title: The Order of the Old Testament — Mario Melendez
item.description: Six approaches to how the Hebrew Bible is arranged, and an argument that the shape of a canon is a theological question and not only a historical one. Narrow, and worth it if the question has ever nagged you.

item.title: Sanctification and the Life of Faith — Kyle C. Strobel & Kent Eilers
item.description: A serious dogmatic treatment of sanctification in the Soteriology and Doxology series. Theology written toward worship rather than away from it.

item.title: Wilderness as a Theme in Biblical Theology — T. Desmond Alexander & Brian S. Rosner
item.description: Wilderness as a Theme in Biblical Theology looks at both the larger picture of Scripture and the specific texts that deal with wilderness themes.

item.title: Church History for Everyone — Kevin DeYoung
item.description: Through 20 extraordinary biographies, Kevin DeYoung explores the fascinating history of the church, helping readers reflect on the bigger story of God's work in the world and gain bold faith for…

item.title: Covenants for Kids — O. Palmer Robertson, illus. Joe Hox
item.description: A color-coded walk through the covenants of the Bible, showing how each one points to Christ.

item.title: The Upside-Down, Inside-Out, Can't-Believe-It Kingdom — Jonathan Landry Cruse, illus. Joe Hox
item.description: A father explains to his son, in rhyme, how God's kingdom works in backward ways: grace, the cross, and being made right with God.

item.title: Reformed Theology — Michael Allen
item.description: Allen's survey of the main doctrines of the Reformed tradition, arranged under eight themes from the Word of God and covenant to worship, confessions and eschatology. This updated paperback edition in T&T Clark's Doing Theology series adds new sections and a new foreword.

item.title: The Last Place in Europe — Geoffrey Plank
item.description: Geoffrey Plank's history of Gibraltar from antiquity to the present: the British capture in 1704, its part in the American Revolution and both World Wars, and the long dispute with Spain.

item.title: Biblical Interpretation, 2nd Edition — Gerald Bray
item.description: Gerald Bray's introduction to the history and practice of interpreting the Bible.

item.title: The Path to the Pulpit — Andrew Hébert & Mitchell L. Chase
item.description: The Path to the Pulpit, by Andrew Hébert and Mitchell L. Chase, offers a practical framework for sermon preparation that helps pastors and ministers view every Scripture passage from all angles.

item.title: Joshua — John D. Currid · Pillar Old Testament Commentary
item.description: A full commentary on Joshua from a veteran Reformed Old Testament scholar and archaeologist — part of Eerdmans' new Pillar Old Testament Commentary series.

item.title: Where the Wild Horses Are — Amy Alznauer
item.description: Twelve-year-old Nash, the hearing daughter of a Deaf family, enters a contest to gentle a wild mustang in one hundred days.

item.title: What Marcel Found — Cedar Pruitt, illus. David Litchfield
item.description: In 1940 a French teenager named Marcel finds a hidden cave full of ancient animal paintings.

item.title: The Story Baker — Carsten Henn
item.description: A ballet dancer whose career ended in injury takes a temporary job at a village bakery and slowly recovers under the old baker's care.

item.title: The Glades — Angela Hunt
item.description: A storm cuts off a family's weekend on a private Everglades island, the caretaker goes missing, and the island's history starts to come out.

item.title: The Flight Nurses' War — Leah Garrett
item.description: Leah Garrett follows a team of American flight nurses who treated and evacuated the wounded from Iwo Jima and Okinawa in 1945.

item.title: Prosperity Road — Anthony J. Badger
item.description: Anthony Badger's one-volume history of the United States from 1920 to 1945: the boom of the twenties, the Crash and Depression, the New Deal, and the war. Sympathetic to Roosevelt.
